fields.note: where the membership came from, and who decided it
§10. What will actually be requested, preserved beside the canonical form
required when the item is excluded, and recorded BEFORE the run

hashing.covers: the manifest as stored, excluding any field carrying the hash itself

immutability.why: the same discipline Mission 1.56 applied to a frozen document: a manifest that no longer answers to the hash a run named is not the population that run measured.

canonical_url_rules.$comment: §10. Canonicalization exists for IDENTITY and de-duplication. What is REQUESTED is stored verbatim, because a contract that normalized the request would measure something the manifest never named.
canonical_url_rules.host_case: lowercased for identity; the requested host is preserved verbatim
canonical_url_rules.idn_punycode: recorded in both forms; the requested form is the one sent
canonical_url_rules.default_ports: omitted from the canonical form; never added to the requested form
canonical_url_rules.path_normalization: dot-segment resolution per RFC 3986 for identity only
canonical_url_rules.fragment: removed, because a fragment is never sent to a server
canonical_url_rules.query_string: preserved exactly where present; see query_string_policy
canonical_url_rules.duplicate_urls: refused at manifest build time rather than silently collapsed
canonical_url_rules.why_not: §10. They are two different requests to two different ports with two different transport contracts, and a construct that wants to treat them as one entity must say so explicitly. Inventing that equivalence here would decide a construct.

query_string_policy.why_stripping_is_forbidden: a stripped query string is a DIFFERENT target, and pretending otherwise would put a measurement of one resource under the identity of another.
query_string_policy.design_preference_for_a_first_pilot: exclude query-bearing URLs unless the corpus requires them and governance approves them, because a query string can carry an identifier or a token
